subject: history_social
passage: The sixth-century historian Procopius of Caesarea wrote an account of the wars of the emperor Justinian that is measured in tone and, in its treatment of campaigns he witnessed in person, generally reliable. He also wrote a treatise praising the emperor's buildings, and a third work, circulated only after his death, in which Justinian and the empress Theodora appear as monsters of greed and cruelty. Because the same writer produced both the praise and the denunciation, historians read neither at face value. The point is not that Procopius invented his material, much of which can be checked against other sources, but that each of these works is ______, shaped to flatter or to wound rather than to weigh.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The final clause defines the blank: each work is "shaped to flatter or to wound rather than to weigh." Writing that is slanted toward a purpose rather than balanced is "tendentious." The text explicitly separates this from inventing material ("not that Procopius invented his material"), so the word must concern bias, not falsehood.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Impartial" means unbiased, the opposite of works written "to flatter or to wound."
explanation.B: Correct. "Tendentious" means written to promote a particular point of view, which fits works shaped to flatter or to wound rather than to weigh.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Apocryphal" means of doubtful authenticity. The text does not question who wrote the works or whether the material is genuine; it says much of it "can be checked against other sources."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Fragmentary" means surviving only in pieces. The text says nothing about the condition of the texts, only about their slant.
